title: Predict how by-value parameters and ref, out, or in affect caller storage

rubric.point: Explains that Position is a value type, so first receives a separate copy and its field change does not change a.
Explains that second aliases b's storage, so changing second.X changes b.X.

questions.model: `a.X` remains `2`; `b.X` becomes `7`. `Position` is a struct, so `b = a` copies its value, and passing `a` by value creates another copy in `first`. Changing `first.X` changes only that parameter's copy. The `ref` parameter `second` aliases `b` itself, so changing `second.X` updates the field stored in `b`.

rubric.point: Identifies the right-hand use of value as a read before the out parameter has been assigned.
Explains that the caller's initialization does not make an out parameter assigned on method entry; the method must assign it before reading it.
Explains that ref permits reading the initialized caller storage and writing the incremented value back, producing score = 21.

questions.model: The right-hand `value` reads the `out` parameter before the method has assigned it. An `out` parameter is treated as unassigned on entry, regardless of whether the caller already stored a value in the argument. With `ref`, the caller must supply initialized storage, and the method may read and write it. The increment would therefore read `20` and store `21` in `score`.

rubric.point: Explains that both parameters alias number's storage, so view observes the assignment through editor rather than retaining a snapshot of 4.
Explains that view = 12 would not compile because in forbids assignment through that parameter, while writes through another writable alias remain possible.

questions.model: It prints `9`. Both arguments explicitly refer to the same `int` variable, so `editor` writes to storage that `view` reads. `in` gives a readonly alias, not a snapshot. Adding `view = 12;` would fail to compile because assignment through `view` is forbidden. That restriction does not prevent the same storage from changing through the writable `ref` alias.
